question: A recent sweep of 314 online sales platforms in 23 EU Member States found that 30 % displayed misleading discounts during Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

Practices that may influence consumers’ purchasing decisions were also found, such as attempts to add items to consumers’ online baskets (36 % of cases) without their consent (4 in 10 cases), failure to explain the reference price so that their prices could be compared at the time of purchase and hiding additional fees such as service or delivery fees until the end of the process (10 % of cases).
Can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What measures does it intend to take to protect consumers from misleading or false discounts and practices such as hidden fees?

In view also of the revision of the Consumer Protection Cooperation Regulation, what options is it considering to ensure more effective cross-border enforcement of EU consumer law, and is it considering the uniform application of sanctions across the EU rather than on a country-by-country basis, particularly in cases of infringements affecting several Member States?
How will it help strengthen the exchange of information between authorities and coordination between EU and national actions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.7.2026) In line with Article 29 of Regulation (EU) 2017/2394 (the Consumer Protection Cooperation (CPC) Regulation)1, the Commission coordinates the sweeps conducted by national authorities.

However, as the responsibility for enforcing consumer protection legislation lies with the Member States, it is for the national authorities to follow up on the findings of the sweep related to individual traders and demand corrective actions as appropriate. Further rules related to misleading practices are under consideration in the context of the Digital Fairness Act2.

In line with the findings of the Commission’s report on the application of the CPC Regulation3, the Commission is exploring measures that enable CPC authorities to act faster and strengthen the CPC system’s deterrent effect, including when enforcing in relation to traders not established in the EU.

The Commission is also assessing the need for centralised investigation and enforcement powers in specific cases at EU level. The Commission ensures swift coordination across EU enforcement systems that complement each other, for example, enforcement under the CPC Regulation and the Digital Services Act4.

In preparation for the revision of the CPC Regulation, the Commission is assessing how this coordination could be further strengthened to ensure consistency, as well as how to strengthen coordination between EU and national actions.
1 Regulation (EU) 2017/2394 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 December 2017 on

cooperation between national authorities responsible for the enforcement of consumer protection laws and repealing Regulation (EC) No 2006/2004, OJ L 345, 27.12.2017, pp. 1-26. 2 https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/14622-Digital-Fairness-Act_en.

3 Report from the Commission to the European Parliament and the Council on the application of Regulation (EU) 2017/2394 of the European Parliament and of the Council on cooperation between national authorities responsible for the enforcement of consumer protection laws, COM(2024)311 final, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:52024DC0311.

4 Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 on a Single Market for Digital Services and amending Directive 2000/31/EC (Digital Services Act), OJ L 277, 27.10.2022, pp. 1-102.
